properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 20 at 9:03AM EDT until October 21 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots, and seas 5 to 8 ft,
highest across the Straits of Florida.

* WHERE...Straits of Florida, Hawk Channel, Gulf waters
including the Dry Tortugas, and Florida Bay.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
swamped bows at reef tract mooring balls, and dragging anchors.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced boaters, especially those with smaller vessels,
should avoid operating in these conditions.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 20 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Tuesday, for the Mon
Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and
fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and
https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Fortymile Country; Upper Tanana Valley; Delta Junction
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 20 at 4:24AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 6 to 12
inches expected, with lower totals of 1 to 3 inches expected from
Northway to the Alcan Border along the Alaska Highway. Locally
higher snow totals of 12 to 16 inches will be possible, especially
between Tanacross and Dot Lake. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.
Rain may mix with snow in the Upper Tanana Valley around Northway
to the Alcan Border.

* WHERE...Delta Junction, Fortymile Country, and Upper Tanana Valley.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Northwest wind gusts may be as high as 35 mph
Tuesday morning through early Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, water, and warm
clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 20 at 4:24AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 5 to 11
inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be a narrow snow gradient. The
highest potential for heaviest snow lies southeast of Fort Yukon.
West and north of there, the likelihood for heavier snow drops
quickly. Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting
closer to 2 to 4 inches or less.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, water, and warm
clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Chatanika River Valley; Fairbanks Metro Area; Nenana
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 20 at 4:24AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 7
inches.

* WHERE...Fairbanks, Fox, Chatanika, Ester and Nenena.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall rates will intensify through Tuesday,
with heavier snow expected by late Tuesday morning. There is high
uncertainty in the exact location of this heavier snow area, as a
band looks likely to set up immediately east of the area. This
detail will be crucial in determining which spots get 6 inches or
more versus 3 inches or less. A 30 mile change east or west will
result in drastic differences. If the area of heavier snow shifts
slightly west, heavy snow becomes more likely over the area, and
some areas like North Pole could see greater totals of 7 or even 8
inches. If the area of heavier snow shifts slightly east, heavy
snow becomes less likely over the area.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Denali Borough.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...North and west of Healy, the chance for heavy
snow drops off quickly due to a narrow gradient of snow. There is
potential for greater than 6 inches in Healy but only a few inches
in Anderson. The exact placement of the area of heavier will have a
dramatic effect on the final snowfall totals. If the band moves a
few dozen miles west, snowfall totals will be on the higher end of

miles east, snowfall totals will likely be on the lower end, even
in Healy.
